candidates.summary: breadcrumb_click analytics stops counting first-segment navigation on every /r/<ns>/ and /p/<ns>/ page: the old <a href="/r/"> moved out of the <ol> the delegate watches, into the popover
candidates.failure_scenario: analytics.ts:76 fires breadcrumb_click on clicks matching ol[data-searchbar-target="breadcrumb"] a. At base the first chip is <a href="/r/"> inside that <ol>. At head it is a <button> in the <ol> and its three links (counterpart, All in <ns>, All realms) sit in div#kind-switch-menu, a sibling of the <ol>. On a gno.land deployment with analytics on, the operator's breadcrumb_click count drops on namespaced pages after deploy with no sign the clicks moved, and the new menu's use is never counted; SIMPLEANALYTICS.md:68 still documents the event as 'Click on any breadcrumb anchor'.
candidates.verify_by: go test the rendered /r/alice/golf/game page for menu anchors with an <ol data-searchbar-target=breadcrumb> ancestor, then click each menu anchor in Chromium with gnoweb's compiled public/js/analytics.js and a stub sa_event: expect breadcrumb_click, observe none
candidates.evidence: Go structure test: 'menu anchors=3, menu anchors matched by breadcrumb_click selector=0, <ol> anchors to /r/=0'. Chromium probe: 'control <ol> anchor /r/alice=breadcrumb_click', 'kind-switch button=none', 'menu /p/alice/golf=none', 'menu /u/alice=none', 'menu /r/=none'.

candidates.summary: the no-anchor-positioning fallback never applies: .b-kind-switch's later inset:auto resets the @supports-not top/left, so the menu opens pinned to the viewport's top-left corner
candidates.failure_scenario: The @supports not (top: anchor(bottom)) block (line 3982) sets top/left, then the .b-kind-switch rule after it at equal specificity sets inset:auto (bundled as left:auto;left:anchor(left);top:auto;top:anchor(bottom)). In a browser without anchor() (Safari before 26, for one) the anchor() declarations are dropped at parse, top:auto/left:auto win, and the popover opens at 0/0 over the gnome logo instead of under the breadcrumb, as the comment above the block promises.
candidates.verify_by: render /r/alice/golf/game, link the committed public/main.css, showPopover() and read the menu's rect in Chromium, once as shipped and once with anchor( renamed xanchor( so the @supports-not branch holds: expect top/left near var(--g-space-14)/var(--g-space-16), observe 0/0
candidates.evidence: shipped: 'fallback @supports active: false', 'menu top/left px: 45/91', 'button bottom/left px: 41/91'. noanchor: 'fallback @supports active: true', 'menu top/left px: 4/0', 'computed top/left: 0px/0px'.

candidates.summary: the first breadcrumb chip was a plain link to the kind listing; it is now a popovertarget button with no fallback, so a browser without the Popover API loses that route
candidates.failure_scenario: On /r/<ns>/... and /p/<ns>/... the 'r'/'p' chip used to be <a href="/r/">. It is now <button popovertarget>; where popover is unsupported (Safari before 17, Chrome before 114, Firefox before 125) the click does nothing and the /r/ or /p/ listing has no breadcrumb route. frontend/package.json targets browserslist 'defaults'; whether that set still holds a popover-less browser is unmeasured.
candidates.verify_by: npx browserslist 'defaults, not ie <= 11' in gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/frontend and check each against caniuse popover; a hit means the chip is dead there
